nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.label: Distribution of the league-longest win streak and the number of tied teams (1/N payout), read from the shared nba.standings_sim path draws
nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.mechanism: The league-longest streak is the maximum over 30 teams of the longest run of consecutive wins in each team's sequence, so a 'longest streak' contract depends on every team's game-by-game win probabilities, their serial dependence, and the chance that two or more teams share the maximum and split the payout. It is computed as a functional of the shared standings_sim paths so streak and win-total contracts are priced from the same draws.
nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.measurement: A view, not a separate simulation: read each team's game-by-game win/loss sequence from the stored paths of the single shared nba.standings_sim run (the same 20,000 season draws, with the same posterior rating draw, home court, rest and injury scenarios that price win totals, seeds and records), and compute on every stored path each team's longest run, with the streak carried in from completed games and counting Cup knockout games before the final but excluding the Cup final, play-in and playoffs. For each team report P(team has the strict maximum), P(team is in the tied set), the distribution of N and E[payout] = E[floor(100/N)/100 * 1{team in the tied set}] as frequencies over those same paths. Do not redraw ratings or games; if the stored paths lack game-level order, extend nba.standings_sim instead. Serial dependence beyond what the shared draw implies (common within-season rating shock) is checked, not re-simulated: compare the simulated league-longest-streak and tie-frequency distribution over the stored paths with the last 15 seasons of real streak lengths and, if they disagree, adjust the shared simulation's game-level dependence so win totals and streaks stay on one set of draws. As-of: nightly with nba.standings_sim; current run for each team carried in.

nba.venue.rationale: League-wide NBA home advantage has been around 2-3 points but has varied and arena-specific effects (altitude, crowd) are small relative to noise, so team-specific home edges should be heavily shrunk. Neutral venues need explicit treatment: only the Cup final (2026-27: Hinkle Fieldhouse), international games and Mexico City/Paris games are neutral; Cup quarterfinals and semifinals are hosted by the higher seed (verified in nba.cup_format), so they carry home court.

nba.live_period_state.label: In-play game state for period and half markets (score, clock, on-court lineups, team fouls, timeouts)
nba.live_period_state.mechanism: Quarter, first-half and second-half markets keep trading after tipoff, so their value is conditional on the realised state at the quote time rather than the pregame distribution.
nba.live_period_state.rationale: Verified on the Kalshi API (9 Nov 2026): KXNBA2H markets for 9 Nov games have close_time 12 Nov 03:00Z, two days after the game, with early close 'after a winner is declared'; KXNBA1Q markets for the 10 Nov OKC-POR game have close_time 13 Nov 04:00Z with the same early-close condition, and a KXNBA1HTOTAL market for the 8 Nov BKN-DAL game carried 'close early if the event occurs' and closed at 02:10:05Z on 9 Nov, well after its open_time (the exact tip time was not read, so how long after tip it stayed open is unverified). Q1 and 1H markets therefore also trade in play once the game starts, while Q1 is still the most pregame-predictable quantity before tip. Prices then depend on the current margin, period, on-court five, team fouls toward the bonus, and timeouts left, none of which a pregame input carries.
